source: BD's own corpus, all public domain: Tao Te Ching (tr. John H. McDonald), Zhuangzi Inner Chapters (tr. James Legge), Grimm's Fairy Tales (tr. Margaret Hunt, 1884), Thomas Hardy, Walt Whitman (Leaves of Grass).
note: 30 Tao / 30 Zhuangzi / 30 Grimm / 15 Hardy / 15 Whitman, interleaved in pairs so that ANY PREFIX covers all five registers -- a reader who stops at 80 still has a balanced set. Selected by phoneme DEFICIT against a target of 14 instances each, not by novelty: covering the inventory is easy and nearly worthless. No utterance contains a word from speech_lexicon.json, nor Tao/Dao: espeak renders those differently from the way a reader says them, and the model would attach her audio to the wrong phonemes. Phonemes these texts cannot supply 14 of are pre-seeded so they are never crowded out; what remains is a limit of the corpus (/ʒ/ x8), and the base voice already knows those, so they stay closer to it than the rest.

reading_notes: Pause about a second before the first word and about two seconds after the last. The rig shows both, and piper keeps only 0.25 s, so the pause protects the cadence of your last word.
Prose and verse are mixed on purpose. Read the Grimm passages as storytelling and the Hardy and Whitman lines as poetry -- a voice that can do both is the whole point of this set.
Read at your normal reading force. Softening the consonants to be safe changes the voice the model learns.
